transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Parker (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (ZephyrSearch), Priya Singh (ZephyrSearch), Omar El-Hadi (ZephyrSearch security)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + reranking for search relevance. Demo of Redwood Console for routing and Optimize suggestions, discussion on latency vs cost, data controls for SOC 2 / VPC, and next steps to run a short pilot/benchmark with anonymized logs.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and vector configs
- Rerank endpoint + candidate ranking flow
- Console: per-route analytics, token cost breakdown, and Optimize recommendations
- Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS for encryption, VPC requirements
- Pilot scope, dataset and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'll kick things off. Liam from our SE team is on to run the technical demo.
[00:12] Daniel Ortiz: Hi, Daniel here, thanks - we have Priya and Omar on as well. We're really looking at improving our relevance without blowing up costs.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Yep, mostly concerned about tail latency and how many queries we can do per second.
[00:27] Liam Parker: Great, quick agenda: how embeddings + rerank work together, live demo on our hosted API and console, then a quick talk about security and pilot next steps. Sound okay?
[00:38] Omar El-Hadi: Yes, and please cover audit logs and encryption - we need to know where logs live.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Briefly to set context - ZephyrSearch current stack Daniel mentioned uses Elastic for indexing and a small BERT rerank in a sidecar, is that right?
[00:55] Daniel Ortiz: Yeah, we've got Elastic for the candidate retrieval and a BERT model on an EC2 for final scoring. It's kinda slow on certain queries.
[01:03] Liam Parker: Cool, so typical pattern: index + vector store for candidate gen, then Redwood Embeddings to produce vectors for queries/documents and Redwood Rerank endpoint to take candidate list plus context and produce a final ordering.
[01:18] Priya Singh: How do you pass the candidates - do you send the full documents?
[01:22] Liam Parker: You usually send the candidate snippets or doc IDs with a small context window. The rerank endpoint takes an array of candidates and returns a score for each. We demo both sending text and sending doc refs with top-k payloads.
[01:34] Daniel Ortiz: What's the cost tradeoff between doing a single larger embedding call vs many small ones?
[01:38] Maya Chen: Good question, generally embedding at index-time and storing vectors reduces query-time cost. For dynamic content we do on-the-fly embeddings for queries only. Cost is per embedding unit and per token for rerank; Optimize gives recommendations to quantize or batch to reduce unit cost.
[01:52] Liam Parker: I'll jump into the console demo now, but quick note - we have prefix caching and KV cache heuristics that help tail latency on long sessions, sorry K V cash in some transcriptions - it's KV cache.
[02:03] Maya Chen: Liam, one clarification: Zephyr has strict data residency, can Redwood host in us-east and eu-west only?
[02:10] Liam Parker: Yes, for hosted we can pin region routing. For stricter residency they sometimes go to Dedicated or Private, but hosted supports region pinning and retention controls.
[02:20] [Screen share shifts] Liam Parker: Ok showing the Console - left panel route config, top shows request metrics, median  p50 p95 latency, tokens per minute, and cost breakdown. Here's an embeddings route configured for 1536-d vectors.
[02:36] Priya Singh: Can we change vector dims? Our embedder is 1024 - will that work?
[02:40] Liam Parker: We support variable dims but recommend standard models - we can host custom or map down/up via transform. We'll note that for the pilot.
[02:47] [00:03:10] Daniel Ortiz: Looks good. Walk us through rerank - how do you ensure the reranker doesn't hallucinate or change semantics?
[03:16] Liam Parker: Rerank uses a scoring head, it doesn't generate free text unless you use a generative rerank mode. For deterministic score-based reranking we apply explainability tokens and allow thresholding. Also you can run A/B tests via rollouts in Console.
[03:33] Priya Singh: Is there a way to get per-token cost by model?
[03:38] Maya Chen: Yes Console shows token-level cost breakdown per model and per route, and Optimize will suggest cheaper model variants when quality delta is acceptable.
[03:45] Omar El-Hadi: Security: what about SSO and audit logs?
[03:49] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO, RBAC roles, and audit logs - logs can be pulled into your SIEM or we can push to a customer-owned S3 for retention. SOC 2 Type II report available; we'll share the doc.
[03:59] Omar El-Hadi: And encryption of data at rest and KMS?
[04:02] Liam Parker: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; for hosted we use envelope encryption and have bring-your-own-key options on enterprise tiers.
[04:12] [04:12] Daniel Ortiz: For the pilot we want to test on a 10k QPS-ish workload for 1 hour and compare p95 latency and relevance metrics (MRR and NDCG). Possible?
[04:24] Liam Parker: That sounds doable with a Dedicated pilot, but we can do a scaled hosted run first as a smoke test. For full 10k QPS we'd recommend Dedicated reserved capacity.
[04:35] Maya Chen: I'll add that to next steps. We'll propose two phases: hosted smoke test with your sample logs, then a short Dedicated pilot if you want to validate scale.
[04:44] [04:44] Priya Singh: About latency numbers - what p95 do you typically see for rerank response if we send top-10 candidates?
[04:52] Liam Parker: For standard rerank with a 7B class model we see p95 ~120-280ms depending on batch mixing. With dedicated GPUs and batching optimizations we can get sub-100ms on average for top-10. The Console shows live p95 and trace hooks to isolate slow requests.
[05:10] Daniel Ortiz: Nice. One more question - how do you handle embeddings versioning?
[05:15] Liam Parker: The model catalog lets you pin embedding versions at index time. You can create new index shards with new vectors or store multiple vectors per doc and route queries to the desired version. Optimize will also call out regressions if new models degrade metrics.
[05:31] [05:31] Maya Chen: Demo time - we'll run a quick example: query -> embeddings endpoint -> nearest neighbors in your vector store (we simulated with a sample dataset) -> call rerank endpoint with top-8 candidates -> show reorder and score.
[05:45] [06:05] Liam Parker: (demo) Sending query "best noise-cancelling headphones" - embeddings returned, nearest neighbor retrieval done, now sending top-8 to rerank. Rendering scores... here's before/after order. Notice that the reranker promotes product pages with better purchase intent.
[06:26] Priya Singh: Does the rerank use document metadata? We need to ensure recency signals are considered.
[06:31] Liam Parker: Yes metadata can be passed and features used in the ranking. We have structured input format for candidate list and per-candidate metadata.
[06:41] [06:41] Daniel Ortiz: This demo looked promising. Any limitations on token length when sending excerpts to rerank?
[06:47] Liam Parker: We recommend excerpt windows less than 1,024 tokens for latency; for large context we use vector context or chunking.
[06:54] Maya Chen: Quick real talk on costs - rerank per-call cost scales with number of candidates and tokens per candidate. Optimize suggests candidate window sizes, model sizes and batching settings to hit your cost/latency target.
[07:08] [07:08] Omar El-Hadi: From a security compliance point, can logs be redacted or filtered before leaving our environment?
[07:14] Liam Parker: For hosted we offer request redaction options and can accept pre-filtered logs; for Private deployments you can keep logs in your VPC entirely. We'll share the specifics.
[07:25] Daniel Ortiz: Ok, what's the simplest path to get a quick comparison against our current BERT sidecar?
[07:30] Maya Chen: Send us anonymized query logs and a small sample dataset. We'll run the hosted smoke test to evaluate relevance metrics and p95 latency, share results and cost estimates. That's the pilot proposal.
[07:40] Priya Singh: Timeline - we can gather logs by early next week.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Great. Liam, any gotchas to call out?
[07:47] Liam Parker: Just watch for mismatch in tokenizer between your index-time pipeline and our embedder; that can shift vector distributions. Also be mindful of deduping content and chunking strategy.
[07:59] [07:59] Daniel Ortiz: Competitors wise, we looked at Algolia recently - cost was high for large vectors - interested to see Redwood's unit economics.
[08:07] Maya Chen: We'll include a cost sheet with the pilot proposal showing per-query estimates across configurations.
[08:12] Priya Singh: Are there SLA options if we move to Dedicated?
[08:16] Maya Chen: Yes Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime tiers plus reserved capacity pricing. We'll include that in the proposal.
[08:25] [08:25] Liam Parker: Quick question from my side - do you need on-prem or VPC for this pilot?
[08:30] Daniel Ortiz: Not for now, hosted is fine for the smoke test, but we need the option for Private later.
[08:36] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll configure region pinning and retention policy for the smoke test.
[08:41] [08:41] (5 minute deep dive into console charts - omitted for brevity in transcript)
[13:45] [13:45] Liam Parker: Jumping back - I'll summarize the technical POC steps we usually follow: 1) ingest sample vectors or provide query logs, 2) Redwood runs hosted smoke test and returns relevance metrics and latency, 3) iterate on candidate window and model size with Optimize, 4) optional Dedicated pilot for scale.
[14:05] Priya Singh: For step 1 we'll provide anonymized logs and document schema.
[14:10] Daniel Ortiz: Also include a short rubric: we care about MRR, NDCG@10, and p95 latency.
[14:15] Maya Chen: Noted - we'll evaluate those metrics.
[14:19] Omar El-Hadi: Please include SOC 2 report and our legal team will need data handling agreement.
[14:23] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC 2 and data processing addendum in the follow-up.
[14:28] [14:28] (small cross-talk, clarifying prediction vs ranking definitions)
[14:40] Daniel Ortiz: Anything else we should be aware of?
[14:43] Liam Parker: For high throughput tests make sure you give us expected QPS patterns and any spike behavior - autoscaling behavior matters.
[14:50] Maya Chen: Ok quick recap and next steps: 1) Redwood sends pricing + pilot proposal (Maya) 2) Redwood shares SOC2 + network architecture + redaction options (Maya) 3) SE to prepare benchmark guide and example dataset instructions (Liam) 4) Zephyr to share anonymized logs and timeframe for smoke test (Daniel/Priya)
[15:10] Daniel Ortiz: Sounds good, we'll aim to have logs by 2026-05-05.
[15:14] Priya Singh: We'll also add expected QPS shapes.
[15:17] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for a technical POC deep-dive.
[15:22] Omar El-Hadi: Thanks.
[15:24] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache) typical of auto-generated speech-to-text. References: demo deck slide 4 (product flow), pilot proposal template (link to be shared), SOC2 report (will share PDF).
